response:
I fixed the bug: the scenario from the issue now runs in 3 queries, and `user.profile.user.kind` no longer triggers a fourth.

**Cause:** When Django prefetches `profile`, the code that builds the prefetch query loops over the Profile results so it can link each profile back to its parent user. That loop is what runs the Profile queryset, so the nested `Prefetch("user", queryset=User.objects.only("kind"))` runs first and caches the correct inner `User` on each profile. The loop then replaces that cached user with the outer one from `User.objects.only("email")`, where `kind` is deferred. That's why `get_deferred_fields()` returned `{'kind'}`.

**Fix:** In `django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`, that back-link step now skips any object whose relation is already cached. I changed it in all three places it happens:
- `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset` (one-to-one, accessed from the side that has the field)
- `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset` (the `user.profile` case in the issue)
- the reverse many-to-one manager's `get_prefetch_queryset` (the ForeignKey / `profile_set` case the issue also mentions)

**Testing:** I wrote two throwaway tests reproducing the one-to-one and ForeignKey cases. Both fail without the change and pass with it. I also ran 388 existing tests (`prefetch_related`, `one_to_one`, `many_to_one`, `foreign_object`, `known_related_objects`, `select_related_onetoone`, `generic_relations`, `contenttypes_tests`), and they all pass. I didn't run the full Django suite. I deleted the throwaway tests, so the only change in the tree is the fix itself.
